title: Meta's Muse Wonder Full Ranks Second on Artificial Analysis Index, Beats OpenAI on Vals

tickers.name: Meta Platforms, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Meta's new Muse Wonder Full model ranked second overall on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 56, trailing only Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 at 58 while beating Claude Fable 5.1 and OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra. The model also debuted at fifth place on the Vals Index, surpassing every OpenAI model and solving 94 of 100 math problems on ProofBench compared with 58 for its predecessor, Muse Spark 1.3. In a separate test across 105 real-world software bugs that frontier models missed in the first quarter, Muse Wonder Full scored 44, behind GPT-6 Astra at 45 and ahead of Fable 5.1 at 43 and Opus 5.5 at 41.7.

The base Muse Wonder model scored 52 on the Artificial Analysis index and is priced on Meta's API at $4 per million input tokens, $0.20 for cached input, and $20 per million output tokens across a 1M token context window. While those token rates match Opus 5.5 and are 60% below GPT-6 Astra and Fable 5.1, heavy input usage of 7.69M tokens per task brings Muse Wonder's average task cost on the benchmark to $4.52, compared with $3.26 for GPT-6 Astra and $5.98 for Opus 5.5. Meta has not released per-token pricing for Muse Wonder Full, which is restricted to paid Muse Code plans.

Meta shares rose as much as 4.7% following Monday's launch and gained another 3.56% to $769.40 on Tuesday as Truist analysts cited early Muse adoption. Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang said late Monday that Meta fixed a launch bug that caused unusually fast quota depletion for Muse Code subscribers and reset user limits. In its model documentation, Meta noted that "visual and spatial reasoning, especially 3D tasks, remains a known limitation," and disclosed that the model captured 71 of 92 cybersecurity benchmark flags via unintended vulnerabilities while requiring safeguards to reduce chemical and biological risks to moderate or lower.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Meta has released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, achieving Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3 scores of 52 and 56 at max reasoning effort - each a material gain over Muse Spark 1.3 (max) at 48
selectedTweets.text:
Meta has released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, achieving Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3 scores of 52 and 56 at max reasoning effort - each a material gain over Muse Spark 1.3 (max) at 48, with a release gap of only 6 weeks

Muse Wonder is available for users on Meta’s first-party API, while Muse Wonder Full is currently only available for Muse Code users. Meta notes that each model is designed for personal and professional agent use

Congratulations to @AIatMeta, @finkd, and @alexandr_wang on the release!

Key Takeaways:

➤ Both models exhibit a material jump in overall Intelligence Index score. Muse Wonder Full (max) improves on Muse Spark 1.3 (max) across all ten Intelligence Index evaluations, gaining 8 points to 56. The largest gains were seen in agentic evaluations: Terminal-Bench 4.0 (+24 points, 33% to 57%), GDPval-AA v2.1 (+176 Elo, 1681 to 1857), and AA-Briefcase (+148 Elo, 1581 to 1729). Muse Wonder (max) gains 4 Intelligence Index points and lands at 52, with notable improvements vs. Muse Spark 1.3 (max) in Terminal-Bench 4.0 (33% to 52%) and AutomationBench-AA (58% to 68%)

➤ Muse Wonder Full (max) places in the top three on six of the ten Intelligence Index evaluations, and is particularly strong in agentic knowledge work and scientific reasoning. In agentic knowledge work, it narrowly leads on GDP.pdf (33%), ranks #2 on GDPval-AA v2.1 (1857 Elo), and #3 on both AA-Briefcase (1729 Elo) and AutomationBench-AA (71%). In scientific reasoning, it tops the CritPt leaderboard at 33% and ranks #3 on SciCode with 63%. This builds on the relative strengths of Muse Spark 1.3 (max), which also showed particular ability in these two domains

➤ Both models use fewer output tokens than Muse Spark 1.3 (max). Muse Wonder (max) and Muse Wonder Full (max) each use around 54k output tokens per Intelligence Index task, down ~10% from Muse Spark 1.3 (max, 60k). This usage is lower than similarly intelligent models Gemini 4 Argon (high, 62k) and Claude Fable 5.1 (max w/ fallback, 78k), but higher than GPT-6.1 Sol (max, 38k) and GPT-6 Astra (max, 27k). Muse Wonder Full (max) uses 16% fewer input tokens per Intelligence Index task than Muse Wonder (max) (6.44M vs 7.69M), meaning it is both more intelligent and more token-efficient

➤ Cost per Task for Muse Wonder (max) lands higher than most similarly intelligent models. Despite efficient output token use, premium API pricing ($4 per million input tokens, $20 per million output tokens) and high input token use (7.69M per task) push Muse Wonder (max)’s cost to $4.52 per Intelligence Index task. This is lower than Claude Fable 5.1 (max w/ fallback, $7.63), Claude Opus 5.5 (max w/ fallback, $5.98), and Claude Sonnet 5.5 (max w/ fallback, $5.46), but higher than GPT-6 Astra (max, $3.26), Gemini 4 Argon (high, $1.99), GPT-6.1 Sol (max, $0.72), and its predecessor Muse Spark 1.3 (max, $1.60). Per-token pricing is not currently available for Muse Wonder Full, so no Cost per Task figure can be estimated at this stage

➤ Both models gain significantly in Coding Agent performance. Muse Wonder Full achieves 68 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agents Index at max effort in Muse Code, alongside Claude Code with Sonnet 5.5 (max, 68) and Opus 5.5 (max, 66). Muse Wonder (max) scores 63. These represent material gains over Muse Code with Muse Spark 1.3 (max), which scores 54

Other details for the two new models:

➤ Context windows: 1M tokens each, unchanged from Muse Spark 1.3
➤ Pricing: for Muse Wonder, $4 input / $0.20 cached input / $20 output per 1M tokens. Pricing per token is not yet announced for Muse Wonder Full
➤ Input modalities: text, image, video, and audio
➤ Output modalities: text
➤ Availability: Muse Wonder is available on Meta's first-party API and Muse Code at launch, while Muse Wonder Full is only available to Muse Code users

selectedTweets.bestBit: This demo uses Muse Wonder to generate a globe web-app from a reference image and prompt. Two agents, same model: (a) a generation main agent, (b) a CUA verification sub-agent.
selectedTweets.text:
Muse Wonder, aka Watermelon is out today!! The consumer use cases of CUA are obvious from Muse, a particular use case I am super bullish about is verification.

CUA offers a feature-complete harness (GUI + code) for the agent to verify its creation, give itself feedback, and self-improve, aka CUA as verification.

This demo uses Muse Wonder to generate a globe web-app from a reference image and prompt. Two agents, same model: (a) a generation main agent, (b) a CUA verification sub-agent. They iterate until the CUA verifier is satisfied. This is an interesting test-time scaling with CUA.

As usual, work done with the incredible CUA and visual coding team at Meta MSL.

@taoyds, @yuning_pro, @EdwardSun0909

selectedTweets.bestBit: now the model can one-shot most IMO problems and even some open research problems
selectedTweets.text:
1. This is an extremely smart and knowledgeable agentic and coding model that excels at personal assistant tasks.  We optimize for personal empowerment, what the users want from AI, rather than automation of jobs. In particular, our model shines on personal finance, personal legal, personal assistant and professional tasks across a wide range of domains.

2. We wanted the model to be an aligned and helpful assistant, so we made the new model significantly better at extremely complicated and long-horizon instruction following.

3. We also did a lot of work to improve model behaviors, similar to humans, model capabilities are measured along two axes: raw intelligence and model behavior. One example of behavior is laziness, like how hard the model tries before giving up. A model can have a lot of knowledge and a high IQ, but it can not achieve great things if it gives up very easily. Our model is trained to be super persistent, and will tirelessly and relentlessly try to complete your tasks / achieve your goals on your behalf.

4. Baking in good model behaviors is challenging. We first need to define and identify good v.s. bad behaviors, and then grade them in order to reinforce them.

5. The model can also exhibit bad behaviors to hack the reward with high enough optimization pressure. We invested a lot in alignment to make the model behaviors safe and sane.

6. The benchmarks might not reflect the usability of the models. Our new model is easy to work with, talk in human languages and no AI slop.

7. We also work really hard to improve core STEM reasoning, now the model can one-shot most IMO problems and even some open research problems. The model can solve much more difficult open problems with scaffolding. We saw people who are not math /physics professors solve interesting problems with our model, this is personal empowerment. Doing math / science research becomes feasible to a much wider audience.
